old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a wok filled with a sizzling stir-fry dish. The wok is metallic and reflective, with steam rising from the food, indicating it is being cooked at high heat. Inside the wok, there are various ingredients including sliced carrots, mushrooms, and what appears to be pieces of chicken or another type of protein. The vegetables are vibrant in color, with the orange of the carrots contrasting against the earthy tones of the mushrooms and the lighter hues of the protein. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the dynamic cooking process. The steam and the movement of the ingredients suggest active stirring, though a metal spatula is visible in the frame. The overall scene conveys a sense of warmth and the appetizing aroma of a freshly prepared meal.

caption: The video captures a close-up view inside a stainless steel wok holding a stir-fry mixture of shredded orange carrots, pale white sprouts, and brown meat strips. A thin metal utensil shaft with a white grip rests at the left edge of the pan, partly buried in the food. A plume of steam rises continuously above the contents, swirling, thinning, and shifting position as the main visible motion. The food pieces themselves stay in essentially the same arrangement throughout the segment, with no stirring or tossing occurring. The camera framing drifts slightly, progressively revealing more of the white utensil grip that is mostly hidden at the left edge. The utensil does not move relative to the food, its growing visibility arising from the framing change rather than object motion. The simmering and steaming of the dish continues steadily across the excerpt.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
